reasons: Classification is correct: Section 16.2 gives Ono (our side) an Array indemnity limited to Array Territory commercialization, Array-sponsored Clinical Studies and Article 15 breaches, with no third-party IP infringement coverage; combined with the Section 15.4 non-infringement disclaimer and the 'own expense' defence allocation in Section 11.4(a), the clause fails even the fallback (licensor IP indemnity with usual exclusions), so a deviation finding rather than compliant/fallback is warranted.

Redline is actionable and minimal in structure: it inserts a new limb (e) into the existing 16.2 list rather than rewriting the section, keeps the existing gross-negligence/wilful-misconduct carve-out applicable, adds the customary Ono-modification/combination exclusions, and expressly overrides Section 11.4 for such claims so the two provisions do not conflict.

The failed regex check ('vendor indemnity for IP infringement present') is a phrasing artefact: the inserted limb sits under the 16.2 chapeau ('Array shall indemnify and hold harmless ... Ono Indemnitees') in p0719, and the new text plainly covers claims that a Product or practice of Array Patents/Know-How 'infringes or misappropriates any intellectual property right of a Third Party'. The 0.688 changed-character ratio reflects a substantive insertion required by the rule, not an unnecessary rewrite.

Comment is accurate, correctly scoped to the customer side, cites the playbook position, and offers a sensible fallback (cap or allocation consistent with 16.4); the rationale also correctly declines to narrow our own 16.1 indemnity, which is already appropriately scoped.

Minor, non-fatal gaps to note rather than flag: the 16.2 chapeau says 'indemnify and hold harmless' without an express duty to defend, and the inserted limb produces slightly awkward list grammar ('and (d) ... , and (e) ...'); neither undermines the fallback position reached.
